newsitem.title: UZBEKISTAN: Uzbek central bank cuts refinancing rate to 40 pct.
newsitem.headline: Uzbek central bank cuts refinancing rate to 40 pct.

text.p: Uzbekistan's central bank said on Tuesday it had cut its annual refinancing rate to 40 percent from January 1, down from 48 percent set in August last year, on expectations of lower inflation.
The Central Bank of Uzbekistan cut its rate after forecasting a decline in inflation to about 30 percent in 1997, the bank said in a statement.

There are no official inflation figures published for 1996, but President Islam Karimov said late last month that he estimated the resource-rich former Soviet republic's 1996 inflation near 60 percent.
The refinancing rate for the first seven months of 1996 was 84 percent.
